title: MasterFabric · On-Prem LLM Stack
tagline: An on-prem LLM platform in one Helm chart on local Kubernetes, with RAG, guardrails and monitoring.
summary: This repo packages an on-prem LLM platform into a single Helm chart running on local Kubernetes (k3d). An open-weight chat model and an embedding model are served behind OpenAI-compatible APIs, a pgvector store holds documentation from other MasterFabric labs, and a RAG API answers questions from that corpus. The API applies layered guardrails at the input, retrieved context and output: pattern rules first, then an LLM risk classifier (Granite Guardian 3.2) for paraphrased attacks the rules miss, with an optional cross-encoder reranker per request. Prometheus and Grafana monitor every component, and quality, guardrails, reranking and load are all measured against the running cluster rather than assumed.
keyResults: Corpus of 23 documents ingested into 207 chunks, with ingest taking 57-58 s (embedding on 1 CPU thread)
Retrieval hit@4 0.933 on 30 questions with a known source, median 0.6 ms in pgvector (HNSW), 46 ms to embed the question
Answer accuracy 0.767 (exact fact in the answer), 5/5 unanswerable questions refused, 0 benign questions blocked, p50 3.56 s end to end (sequential)
Guardrails, rules only (v1.0): 22/26, with 18/18 injection/extraction/jailbreak/delimiter/encoded/exfiltration prompts blocked and 4/4 PII prompts masked, but 0/4 paraphrase evasions caught
Guardrails + LLM classifier (v1.1): 24/26, with evasions 4/4 blocked, but 2/4 PII questions now blocked too (false positives); 0/35 benign questions blocked; classifier p50 1.17 s on CPU
Held-out attacks (written before the classifier): rules 0/16 -> rules + classifier 10/16, hard benign questions blocked 1/14, threshold 0.6 fixed on the dev set
Guard v1.2 on a fresh held-out set (24 attacks, 20 hard benign questions): attacks caught 18/24 -> 22/24, benign blocked 2/20 -> 4/20; kept optional, v1.1 stays the default
Guard v1.2 (override_narrow at 0.55) on dev: 22/22 attacks caught, 2/39 benign blocked, same as v1.1; on held-out v1 (used to select it): 14/16 caught, 1/14 blocked
Guard v1.2 control, not used to choose: v1.1's definition at threshold 0.55 gets 21/24 caught and 3/20 blocked on the fresh set, so most of the gain is the lower threshold

RAG judge (Qwen2.5-7B, RAGAS-style, 30 answerable questions): faithfulness 0.967 (vector) and 0.817 (reranked), 0.917 after reading the negatives by hand; context precision 0.650 -> 0.878 with the reranker; context recall 0.967 -> 1.000

RAG judge sanity: faithfulness 0.18-0.28 against another question's contexts; recall agrees with string matching on 97-100% of questions; 3 of its 8 negative verdicts were wrong; 360 judge calls took 10 minutes
Reranker (bge-reranker-v2-m3): hit@1 0.833 -> 0.933, hit@4 0.933 -> 1.000, answer accuracy unchanged at 0.800, +3.8 s p50 on CPU
LLM load test (k6, in-cluster): 1 user 1.57 req/s at 96 output tok/s; 4 users 4.1 req/s at 160 tok/s; 8 users 174 tok/s at p95 3.05 s
RAG load test: best 3.97 req/s at 2 users (p95 0.76 s); at 8 users, 1.33 req/s with p95 9.5 s
Guardrail path alone handles about 5,000 blocked requests/s with p50 3.2 ms at 16 users
limitations: No GPU, no vLLM run: the Docker VM on Apple Silicon cannot reach the GPU, so the vLLM path is rendered and linted but not executed; all throughput figures are CPU figures for a 1.5B model
Small model: Qwen2.5-1.5B answers 77% of questions correctly and cites passages in only 23% of answers, even with retrieval at 93%; a 7B+ model on a GPU is the expected fix but not measured here

Evaluation size: 35 questions and 26 attacks from one corpus give a direction, not a benchmark; accuracy is string matching of an accepted fact, which can miss a correct paraphrase; the prompt was changed once after the first run (both runs reported)

Guardrails are rules plus one classifier: rules alone catch 0/4 dev evasions and 0/16 held-out attacks; with the classifier, 4/4 and 10/16, at the cost of 2/4 PII and 1/14 hard benign questions blocked; several catches are within 0.02 of the threshold and the classifier adds about 1.2 s per question on CPU; only the input is classified, answers are not, and the indirect-injection path was not exercised end to end; guard v1.2 catches 22/24 attacks of a fresh set but blocks 4/20 benign questions, and no definition change separated the two better, only shifted the trade-off; adaptive attacks were not tried
The RAG judge is a model too: 3 of its 8 negative verdicts were wrong, it is from the same family as the generator (possible self-preference, not measured), and 30 questions on one corpus is small
Guard memory limit raised, not re-tested: 4 GiB follows an OOMKill at 3 GiB; no load test since
Reranker does not help answers here: better ranking (hit@1 0.83 -> 0.93) gave the same answer accuracy on 30 questions at +3.8 s, measured on CPU with a 1.5B generator only
Run-to-run variation: the v1.1 quality run with the classifier answered 0.800 versus 0.767 for the v1.0 run with the same prompt, a difference traced to one question (q20) rather than the classifier
Memory: the guard and rerank servers add about 4.5 GiB of memory limits, so the stack now needs Docker with about 10 GB
Monitoring is a lab setup: metrics live in an emptyDir for 2 days, there are no alert rules, and Grafana allows anonymous viewers on a port-forward
Load test caveat: the question pool is small, so the prompt cache flatters low-concurrency RAG numbers; stages run 30 s on one node alongside other containers

Single node with no HA for pgvector or the model servers (PDB and HPA are defined but scaling is bounded by 6 vCPUs); the ingress is HTTP on loopback without authentication; the pgvector password is generated in-cluster and never stored in git
